briefdescription.para: Used to notify the internal state of a processor resource.

detaileddescription.para: A processor resource is available if it is not reserved, and there are available slots in the buffer. A processor resource is unavailable if it is either reserved, or the associated buffer is full. A processor resource with a buffer size of -1 is always available if it is not reserved.
Values of type ResourceStateEvent are returned by method ResourceManager::canBeDispatched()

The naming convention for resource state events is:
Event names start with prefix RS_
Prefix RS_ is followed by a string describing the actual resource state.

detaileddescription.para: This is used to identify a specific processor resource unit using a pair of indices where the 'first' index is a processor resource mask, and the 'second' index is an index for a "sub-resource" (i.e. unit).

briefdescription.para: Populates vector Masks with processor resource masks.

detaileddescription.para: The number of bits set in a mask depends on the processor resource type. Each processor resource mask has at least one bit set. For groups, the number of bits set in the mask is equal to the cardinality of the group plus one. Excluding the most significant bit, the remaining bits in the mask identify processor resources that are part of the group.
ResourceA Mask: 0b001 ResourceB Mask: 0b010 ResourceAB Mask: 0b100 U (ResourceA::Mask | ResourceB::Mask) == 0b111

ResourceAB is a processor resource group containing ResourceA and ResourceB. Each resource mask uniquely identifies a resource; both ResourceA and ResourceB only have one bit set. ResourceAB is a group; excluding the most significant bit in the mask, the remaining bits identify the composition of the group.
Resource masks are used by the ResourceManager to solve set membership problems with simple bit manipulation operations.

briefdescription.para: Compute the reciprocal block throughput from a set of processor resource cycles.

detaileddescription.para:
The reciprocal block throughput is computed as the MAX between:
NumMicroOps / DispatchWidth
ProcReleaseAtCycles / #ProcResourceUnits (for every consumed resource).
